description:
This session will provide an overview of good practices for increasing the longevity of your personal digital archives such as digital photographs, web content, AV materials, research and creative projects.

For those who would like a general introduction to research data management, please consider attending the [[ONLINE] Introduction to Research Data Management](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4026868) workshop scheduled for August 24 and [[ONLINE] Introduction to Data Management Plans](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4026869) on August 25. title: [ONLINE] Personal Digital Archiving

description:
Research data management, or RDM, is increasingly recognized as an important part of the research enterprise in all disciplines. With the introduction of the [Tri-Agency Research Data Management Policy](https://science.gc.ca/eic/site/063.nsf/eng/h_97610.html), and the broad recognition of principles such as [FAIR](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/), [CARE](https://www.gida-global.org/care), and [OCAP](https://fnigc.ca/ocap-training/), it’s crucial for anyone conducting research to understand and adopt good RDM practices. This workshop will give you an overview of the essentials of RDM, including information about sharing and depositing data, managing sensitive data, and data management plans (DMPs).

This session is primarily intended for graduate students, faculty, postdoctoral fellows, and staff engaged in research outside of the classroom setting. For undergraduate students conducting research for a class, please contact your [subject librarian](https://library.ucalgary.ca/services/mylibrarian#find-librarians).

For those who would like a more in-depth session on DMPs, please consider also attending the [Introduction to Data Management Plans workshop](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4026869) on August 25. For information on other skills, principles, and UCalgary services related to RDM, please consider the following workshops:

- [Research Ethics with Human Participants](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/calendar/lcr-workshops/researchethics) on August 24
- [Personal Digital Archving](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4029141) on August 24
- [Beyond the Desktop: Advance your research with Supercomputers](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4030631) on August 25
- [Digital File Management](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/calendar/lcr-workshops/filemanagement2026) on August 26
title: [ONLINE] Introduction to Research Data Management

description:
Learn to read and write R scripts for computations, data manipulation, and simple analysis. You will get hands-on coding experience via a web application, no software installation is required to attend. The goal is to explain the rules of the R syntax in general terms so you can make more sense of an introductory book or the recipes you will find when searching for solutions online. This tutorial is full of short exercises and code examples. It is directed to undergraduate or graduate students interested in learning R to apply it in assignments, projects, or theses but with no programming experience.

Part 1 (Aug 25 @ 4) covers using operators, expressions, variables, and built-in functions in R. Understanding assignment and how arguments work when calling functions. The data types and structures R offers to model data. Introduction to vectors. Part 2 (Aug 26 @ 4) covers the remaining data structures to model and manipulate data: factors, matrices, arrays, lists, and finally, the workhorse of data analysis, the data frame. We will study the basics of subsetting and ordering for data structures. Finally, we will have a look at user functions and basic control flow.  
  
Please contact jdlbrosz@ucalgary.ca if you wish to attend but do not have a UCalgary email address for registration.
title: Introduction to R syntax: part 1: operators, expressions, variables, built-in functions, arguments, data types, vectors

description:
When you're working on incorporating good research data management (RDM) practices into your research, a data management plan, or DMP, is a crucial tool to ensuring you can keep everything organized, both during and after your project. DMPs are also increasingly being required as part of funding applications, including those for the [Tri-Agencies](https://science.gc.ca/site/science/en/interagency-research-funding/policies-and-guidelines/research-data-management/tri-agency-research-data-management-policy). This workshop will examine the key questions to consider when preparing a DMP, and will introduce the [DMP Assistant](https://dmp-pgd.ca/) online tool for preparing your plan.

This session is primarily intended for graduate students, faculty, postdoctoral fellows, and staff at UCalgary engaged in research outside of the classroom setting. For undergraduate students conducting research for a class, please contact your [subject librarian](https://library.ucalgary.ca/services/mylibrarian#find-librarians).

For those who would like a general introduction to research data management, please consider attending the [Introduction to Research Data Management](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4026868)workshop on August 24. For information on other skills, principles, and UCalgary services related to RDM, please consider the following workshops:

- [Research Ethics with Human Participants](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/calendar/lcr-workshops/researchethics) on August 24
- [Personal Digital Archving](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4029141) on August 24
- [Beyond the Desktop: Advance your research with Supercomputers](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/event/4030631) on August 25
- [Digital File Management](https://workrooms.ucalgary.ca/calendar/lcr-workshops/filemanagement2026) on August 26

description:
**Workshop: Depositing Research Data to Borealis, the Canadian Dataverse Repository**

This hands-on workshop, delivered by the [UBC Library Research Data Management team](https://researchcommons.library.ubc.ca/the-team/), guides participants through the process of depositing datasets into the UBC Borealis collection. Designed for graduate students, researchers, and staff, the session emphasizes best practices for sharing and preserving data in alignment with institutional and funder requirements.

**Participants will learn how to:**

- Prepare and organize research data and documentation for deposit into Borealis
- Navigate the Borealis platform and complete metadata fields effectively
- Apply licensing, access controls, and versioning to support open, ethical, and reusable data sharing

 

#### Location: ONLINE

(A Zoom link will be sent to registrants 3 hours before the event starts.)
title: Data Bites - Depositing Research Data to Borealis, the Canadian Dataverse Repository

description:
This session will provide researchers with practical tools and strategies for assessing the scientific and societal impact of their published datasets. Participants will be introduced to tools such as DataCite Commons, the Data Citation Index, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), Altmetric, and PlumX Metrics.

The TCA Lunch and Learn Series is an informal, engaging learning opportunity designed to foster professional development, build capacity, spark curiosity, and encourage cross-functional collaboration. Hosted monthly, each session features an internal expert or guest speaker who shares insights on a wide range of topics. These sessions are:

- ** Accessible and relaxed**, allowing participants to learn in a casual setting.

-  **Interactive**, with opportunities for Q&A and discussion.

- ** Diverse in content**, reflecting the interests and expertise of our vibrant TCA community.

-  **Open to all**, encouraging participation across departments and roles.

Presented by Pierre-Emmanuel Roy, Research Support Librarian, Université du Québec à Rimouski

\*\*\*

Cette séance introduira le personnel de recherche à des outils et des stratégies pratiques pour évaluer l’impact scientifique et sociétal de leurs jeux de données publiés. Cette initiation présentera des outils tels que DataCite Commons, Data Citation Index, Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), Altmetric et PlumX Metrics.

La série _Lunch and Learn_ du programme Transformer l'action pour le climat (TAC) propose des activités d’apprentissage informelles et stimulantes conçues pour favoriser le développement professionnel, renforcer les compétences, susciter la curiosité et encourager la collaboration transversale. Les séances portent sur un large éventail de sujets et sont animée par des expertes et experts affiliés au programme TCA ou invités. Ces séances sont :

- **Accessibles et décontractées**, permettant d’apprendre dans un cadre informel.

- **Interactives**, avec des occasions de questions-réponses et d’échanges.

- **Diversifiées dans leur contenu**, reflétant les intérêts et l’expertise de la communauté dynamique du programme TCA.

- **Ouvertes à toutes et à tous**, favorisant la participation de l’ensemble des disciplines et des rôles.

Présenté par Pierre-Emmanuel Roy, bibliothécaire en soutien à la recherche, Université du Québec à Rimouski
keywords: Activités du PBUQ > Gestion des données de recherche
title: Measuring the impact of datasets

description: This workshop is open to all applicants. However, CSAFS ICT participants receive acceptance priority and a discounted registration rate.   Microbes are everywhere and the study of microbiomes has become a multidisciplinary science involving microbiology, statistics, computer science, and molecular biology to elucidate the impact of microbes in various ecosystems, including the human body. Microbiomics, the study of microbes without first culturing and isolating the organisms, has become the principal approach to exploring the diversity, function and ecology of microbial communities.  This 3-day course provides an introduction to marker-gene analysis, metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data analysis followed by hands-on practical tutorials for each session to demonstrate the use of relevant bioinformatics and statistical tools. Modules will consist of lectures covering both theoretical and practical components followed by hands-on bioinformatic tutorials guided by instructors and teaching assistants.
prerequisites: Experience with UNIX and R/Python programming languages. Included with this workshop is a virtual pre-session (August 26-28) that covers this prerequisite. You will require your own laptop computer. Minimum requirements: 1024×768 screen resolution, 2.4GHz CPU, 8GB RAM, 100GB free disk space, recent versions of Windows, Mac OS X or Linux (Most computers purchased in the past 3-4 years likely meet these requirements). This workshop requires participants to complete pre-workshop tasks and readings.
title: (2026) CBW/CS-DCC Microbiome Analysis: Guelph, ON

description:
This workshop will introduce participants to the [Digital Research Alliance of Canada (the Alliance)](https://www.alliancecan.ca/en). The Alliance supports Canadian researchers in the areas of advanced research computing, research data management and research software. The Alliance also provides access to cloud computing and high-performance computing. Participants will be guided through the process of accessing these resources, and of getting support when using them. Throughout the workshop, participants will learn why and how ARC is useful in the humanities and social sciences.

Instructor: [Maria Sigridur Finnsdottir](https://mariasfinnsdottir.ca/) is the Humanities and Social Sciences Specialist with the Digital Research Services team at the University of Alberta. She holds a PhD in Sociology awarded from the University of Toronto in 2024. She is also the chair of the national HSS team at the Digital Research Alliance of Canada.

For more training opportunities in the 2026-27 HSS Training Series, visit [this page](https://hss-nt.github.io/training/#intro-en).

-------------
Cet atelier présentera aux participants [l’Alliance de recherche numérique du Canada] (https://www.alliancecan.ca/en). L’Alliance soutient les chercheurs canadiens dans les domaines du calcul scientifique avancé, de la gestion des données de recherche et des logiciels de recherche. Elle offre également un accès à l’informatique en nuage et au calcul haute performance. Les participants seront guidés dans le processus d’accès à ces ressources et dans l’obtention de soutien lors de leur utilisation. Tout au long de l’atelier, ils découvriront l’utilité de l’ARC en sciences humaines et sociales.

Formatrice ou formateur: [Maria Sigridur Finnsdottir](https://mariasfinnsdottir.ca/) est spécialiste de sciences humaines et sociales au sein de l'équipe des services de recherche numérique de l'Université de l'Alberta. Elle a obtenu un doctorat en sociologie à l'Université de Toronto en 2024. Elle préside également l'équipe nationale SHS de l'Alliance de recherche numérique du Canada.

Pour découvrir d’autres formations de la série HSS 2026-2027, consultez [cette page⁠](https://hss-nt.github.io/training/fr/)
organizer: Digital Research Alliance of Canada -  National Humanities and Social Sciences Team
title: Introduction to the Alliance & ARC for HSS
